title: Sky Governance can re-enable an Agent's token emissions when the Agent breaches Risk Capital requirements
content:
The same provision that permanently disables AGENT7 emissions adds one exception: "Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Launch Agent 7 is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework" (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.2.1.1.6, referencing A.3.2 - Risk Capital).

This makes the word *permanently* jurisdictional rather than absolute. The lock is unconditional against the Agent and conditional against the ecosystem — a two-tier immutability where the party with the incentive to dilute is bound and the party with the mandate to protect solvency is not.

The carve-out reveals what dilution is being reserved for: recapitalization. Minting new Agent tokens is being kept available as a tool for restoring Risk Capital, i.e. forcing existing holders to absorb a shortfall rather than letting it propagate into Sky. Agent-token holders are therefore the designated first-loss layer, and the emissions lock is the mechanism that ensures they can only be diluted for that reason.

There is a live tension here worth naming: the two conditions ("in violation of Risk Capital requirements" *and* "emissions are required by the Risk Framework") are both defined outside this Artifact, so the durability of the supply guarantee depends on documents the Agent does not control.
description: The single carve-out to permanently disabled emissions: if the Risk Framework requires emissions to cure a Risk Capital violation, Sky Governance may revert the lock the Agent itself cannot touch.
